channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: Vapers ‘blindsided’ by potential 264% price hike as new vape duty looms
item.description: A 264% price hike is not a small adjustment for people who have moved from smoking to vaping. Price can decide whether a lower-risk product remains usable, especially for adults managing dependence, budgets and the temptation to return to cigarettes. Vape duty should not make the safer legal option feel like a luxury or push consumers towards cheaper illicit products. Tax policy needs to support the shift away from combustion, not penalise it. (Published on September 29, 2026byasiantrader.biz)

item.title: Public health fails in ways it can’t even see
item.description: Public health can fail quietly when it counts intentions more carefully than consequences. Campaigns, restrictions and official messages may be designed to protect people, yet still produce confusion, mistrust or worse choices in the real world. Nicotine policy is a clear example: caution becomes harmful when it hides the difference between smoking and lower-risk alternatives. A stronger public health culture would measure what its advice actually does, not only what it was meant to do. (Published on September 29, 2026bydrvinayprasad.com)

item.title: Cliff Douglas: Risk Continuum Should Play a Central Role in Tobacco Policy
item.description: The risk continuum should be central to tobacco policy because not all nicotine products carry the same harm. Cigarettes sit at the highest end because they burn tobacco, while smoke-free alternatives can reduce exposure for adults who switch completely. That distinction is not a technical detail; it is the basis for proportionate regulation, honest communication and better choices for smokers. Tobacco policy becomes more effective when it reflects levels of risk instead of treating nicotine as one category. (Published on September 29, 2026by2firsts.com)

item.title: How to win the vote of generation vape
item.description: Vaping policy should not depend on which party finds it useful in a campaign cycle. Adult smokers need clear information, legal lower-risk options and safeguards that keep products away from young people. Turning vaping into a partisan symbol risks flattening the evidence into slogans, whether the aim is tougher restriction or faster authorisation. The real test is simpler: does the policy reduce smoking-related harm while keeping the market accountable? (Published on September 29, 2026bythehill.com)

item.title: New Nicotine Products & Cardiovascular Health: What Does the Evidence Say? | #GFN26 Science Lab
item.description: Cardiovascular risk is one of the places where nicotine policy needs the most precision. New nicotine products should be assessed by what they do to exposure, biomarkers and real-world switching, not by assuming every product carries the same risk as smoking. Cigarettes remain uniquely harmful because combustion drives a major share of cardiovascular damage. The evidence debate should help smokers understand relative risk clearly, while still recognising uncertainty where the science is still developing. (Published on September 29, 2026bygfn.tv)
